mainTopic: A divorce after giving property to הקדש, or with a guarantor for the כתובה: the worry of קינוניא, the debate over why רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree, and the story of רב הונא.
overview: The משנה discusses a man who gave all his property to הקדש while he still owes his wife her כתובה. רבי אליעזר says that if he divorces her, he must make a נדר הנאה so he cannot remarry her. רבי יהושע says this is not needed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל applies the same worry to a ערב (guarantor) for the כתובה. The גמרא first explains that the argument is about whether people plot (קינוניא) against הקדש. It answers רב הונא's ruling about a dying man by limiting the argument to a healthy person. Next it tries explaining the argument through vows made in public or על דעת רבים. It rejects those explanations because of אמימר's ruling and רבי יהושע's wording "אינו צריך." It concludes that the argument is about undoing a הקדש through שאלה, and a ברייתא links this to בית שמאי and בית הלל on הקדש made by mistake. Finally, a story tells of אביי's idea to help the poor רב הונא get money from his father, who had guaranteed the כתובה. The גמרא discusses רבא's objection, whether the advice was proper, and whether a guarantor of a כתובה must pay at all. That last question is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: A man consecrates his property while owing his wife's כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a disagreement. רבי אליעזר says a man who was מקדיש his property must vow off benefit from his wife when he divorces her. רבי יהושע says he does not need to.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone consecrates all his property while he still owes his wife her כתובה, רבי אליעזר says that when he divorces her, he must vow not to benefit from her. רבי יהושע says he does not have to.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a case where all of a man's property went to הקדש but his wife's כתובה is still owed. רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about whether a divorce here needs a special vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife's כתובה is a debt, so she can collect it from the property, even though it now belongs to הקדש. רבי אליעזר worries the couple might divorce only so she can collect from הקדש, and then remarry. So he requires a vow that forbids the husband to benefit from her, which blocks the remarriage. רבי יהושע sees no need for this.

keyTerms.meaning: One who consecrates, meaning he gives property to the Temple treasury
Property, possessions
The marriage contract money a husband owes his wife if he divorces her
A vow forbidding benefit from someone

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who consecrates his property
and there was upon him a woman's marriage contract,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
when he divorces her, he shall vow off benefit,
phrases.notes: He vows not to benefit from her, so he can never remarry her.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: he need not.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ נְכָסָיו וְהָיְתָה עָלָיו כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the husband must make a נדר הנאה when he divorces. רבי יהושע: no vow is needed.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the same worry with a guarantor
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל applies the same worry to a guarantor (ערב) for a כתובה. The husband must vow off benefit, so the couple cannot plot against the guarantor's money.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a similar way, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: even when someone guaranteed a woman's כתובה and her husband is divorcing her, the husband must vow off benefit from her. Otherwise they might plot against the guarantor's property, and then he would take his wife back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a parallel case. A third person promised to pay the כתובה, and the same plot could be used against that person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'victim' of the plot is a private person, the ערב, and not הקדש. The fear is the same: a fake divorce, the wife collects, and then they remarry. The vow makes remarriage impossible, so the plot would not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Similarly, in a matching case
A guarantor, someone who promises to pay another person's debt
A plot or scheme between two people to take someone else's money

steps.whyThisMatters: The word קינוניא (plotting) becomes the key idea of the whole גמרא that follows.

phrases.english: On a similar note,
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
even the guarantor for a woman for her marriage contract,
and her husband was divorcing her,
the husband must be bound by a vow off benefit from her,
lest he make a plot
against the property of this one,
and he will take his wife back.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בְּדָבָר אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case that uses the same reasoning as רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a guarantor backs the כתובה, the divorcing husband must vow off benefit, to prevent קינוניא against the guarantor.

steps.title: What is the root of the argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking what idea lies under the argument in the משנה. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only gives the rulings, not the reasons. The גמרא wants to find the exact point where the two תנאים split.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asks for the root idea of an argument)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the argument in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

steps.title: Do people plot against הקדש?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that a person would plot even against הקדש. רבי יהושע holds that a person would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds that a person would plot against הקדש. רבי יהושע holds that a person would not plot against הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The argument is about whether we suspect people of scheming to take money from הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether people would be afraid to cheat הקדש. רבי אליעזר does not trust them even there, so he requires the vow. רבי יהושע assumes people would not cheat הקדש, so no vow is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated property belonging to the Temple treasury
Holds, is of the opinion

steps.whatToRemember: The argument is not about divorce. It is about whether we suspect people of plotting against הקדש: רבי אליעזר says yes, רבי יהושע says no.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds:
a person makes a plot against the Temple treasury,
and Rabbi Yehoshua holds:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה קִינוּנְיָא עַל הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ.
phrases.english: a person does not make a plot against the Temple treasury.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה קִינוּנְיָא עַל הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two disagree about whether people would make קינוניא against הקדש.

steps.title: רב הונא's ruling seems to take a side in the argument
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a dying man who was מקדיש everything is believed when he says he owes someone a מנה, because people do not plot against הקדש. The גמרא asks: did רב הונא simply follow רבי יהושע against רבי אליעזר?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what about רב הונא's ruling? A dying man consecrated all his property and said, 'I owe so-and-so a מנה.' He is believed, because we assume people do not plot against הקדש. Should we say רב הונא's ruling follows one side of a dispute between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. רב הונא's ruling uses the same idea as רבי יהושע, so it would seem to go against רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument in the משנה is about plotting against הקדש, then רב הונא's reason (חזקה that no one plots against הקדש) matches only רבי יהושע. The גמרא does not like to say an אמורא's ruling stands on only one side of a מחלוקת of תנאים, so it raises this as a difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is dangerously ill, on his deathbed
A sum of one hundred זוז
Believed, trusted
A presumption, what we assume to be true
Shall we say it is like a dispute of תנאים? (it would match only one side)

steps.confusionAlert: The dying man's claim would take money away from הקדש and give it to the person he named. We might suspect the two of them were working together, and רב הונא says we do not suspect this.

phrases.english: But then, that which Rav Huna said:
a dying man who consecrated all his property,
and said: 'So-and-so has a maneh in my hand' — he is believed,
phrases.notes: 'In my hand' means 'I owe it to him.'

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָקָה אֵין עוֹשֶׂה קִינוּנְיָא עַל הֶקְדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: since there is a presumption that one does not plot against the Temple treasury,
shall we say he stated his teaching according to one side of a dispute of tanna'im?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the explanation of step 4 to find a problem with רב הונא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling about the שכיב מרע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אליעזר holds that people do plot against הקדש, then רב הונא's reason fits only רבי יהושע and is disputed.

steps.title: Everyone agrees about a dying man
steps.stepSummary: No. The argument is only about a healthy person. With a dying man, everyone agrees he would not plot, because a person does not sin when he gains nothing from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. They argue only about a healthy person. But with a dying man, everyone agrees that a person does not plot against הקדש. Why? Because a person does not sin for nothing in return.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב הונא fits both תנאים. The משנה's argument is only about a healthy man, while רב הונא's case is a dying man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy husband gains from the plot, because he gets his wife back along with the money. So רבי אליעזר suspects him. A dying man gains nothing for himself, so even רבי אליעזר agrees he would not sin just to help someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue as far as this case (it limits the argument)
A healthy person
Everyone agrees
A person does not sin when it brings no benefit to himself

steps.whatToRemember: The argument about plotting against הקדש applies only to a healthy person, who gains from the plot. A dying man gains nothing, so everyone agrees he is trusted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רב הונא's ruling true for everyone. It also teaches a general rule: we suspect people of sinning only when they benefit from it.

phrases.english: No, they disagree only
about a healthy person,
but with a dying man, everyone agrees

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה קִינוּנְיָא עַל הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ.
phrases.english: a person does not make a plot against the Temple treasury.
What is the reason?
A person does not sin when it is not for himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא בְּבָרִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by limiting the argument to a healthy person.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the מחלוקת applies only to a בריא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא's ruling seemed to follow only רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a שכיב מרע everyone agrees there is no קינוניא, because אין אדם חוטא ולא לו. So רב הונא fits all opinions.

steps.title: Another version: they argue about a vow made in public
steps.stepSummary: Some say that for a healthy person, the plotting question is not the dispute. Instead, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about whether a vow made in public can be undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: with a healthy person, everyone agrees about the plotting question. Here they argue about a vow made in public. One holds it can be undone, and the other holds it cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new answer to the question from Step 3 about what the two sages really argue about. This time the argument is about vows, not about plotting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides now worry that the couple might plot. רבי יהושע says a vow made in public can still be undone, so making the husband vow does not help. רבי אליעזר says such a vow cannot be undone, so the vow does protect against plotting.

keyTerms.meaning: Plotting or collusion to trick someone out of money
A vow made in public, in front of many people
Undoing a vow. Here it means having it released by a חכם

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this line as saying nobody worries about plotting. In this version both sides do worry about plotting. They only argue about whether the husband's public vow can be undone.

phrases.english: Some say:
With a healthy person, everyone does not argue
phrases.notes: So even with a healthy man, the earlier answer from Step 4 is being dropped.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה קִינוּנְיָא עַל הֶקְדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: about 'a person does not plot against הקדש,'
phrases.notes: He means plotting is not what they argue about. As the next lines show, both sides here worry about plotting.

phrases.english: and here they argue about a vow made in public.
One master holds: it can be undone,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהושע, who says making the husband vow is useless, since the vow can be undone.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: it cannot be undone.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר, who therefore requires the vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of Steps 4 and 6 with a different explanation of the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle do רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about (from Step 3)?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether a vow made in public can be undone.

steps.title: Another option: they argue about a vow made on the public's consent
steps.stepSummary: Or say instead: everyone agrees a public vow can be undone. They argue about a vow made על דעת רבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: everyone agrees a vow made in public can be undone. Here they argue about a vow made on the consent of the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers yet another way to explain the argument. Now both sides agree about public vows, and the argument moves to vows made על דעת רבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow made על דעת רבים is tied to the public's consent. רבי אליעזר holds it cannot be undone, so the vow works. רבי יהושע holds even this can be undone, so the vow is useless.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
On the consent of the public: a vow tied to the agreement of many people

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
everyone agrees that a vow made in public
can be undone,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּנֶדֶר שֶׁהוּדַּר עַל דַּעַת רַבִּים
phrases.english: and here, about a vow made on the consent of the public,
they argue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second vow-based explanation, moving the argument from a public vow to a vow made על דעת רבים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle do רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether a vow made על דעת רבים can be undone.

steps.title: Challenge: אמימר's ruling would become a matter of argument
steps.stepSummary: אמימר ruled that a public vow can be undone but a vow על דעת רבים cannot. According to Step 8, this would be a תנאים argument, which is hard to accept.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about אמימר's statement: a vow made in public can be undone, and one made on the public's consent cannot be undone? Shall we say he stated his teaching according to only one side of a תנאים argument?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from Step 8. It brings אמימר's clear ruling and points out that it would end up depending on an argument between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר states his rule as simple fact. If רבי יהושע held that even a vow על דעת רבים can be undone, then אמימר would just be siding with רבי אליעזר. The גמרא finds it unlikely that אמימר's plain ruling is really only one side of an argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute of תנאים: depends on an argument between sages of the משנה
His teaching or ruling

phrases.english: But then, that which אמימר said:

phrases.aramaic: נֶדֶר שֶׁהוּדַּר בָּרַבִּים יֵשׁ לוֹ הֲפָרָה,
phrases.english: a vow made in public can be undone,

phrases.aramaic: עַל דַּעַת רַבִּים אֵין לוֹ הֲפָרָה —
phrases.english: one made on the public's consent cannot be undone:
shall we say he stated his teaching according to one side of a תנאים argument?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation of Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the sages argue about a vow made על דעת רבים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It would make אמימר's plain ruling depend on a תנאים argument, siding against רבי יהושע.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יהושע's wording does not fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע said the husband "does not need" to vow. If the vow were useless because it can be undone, he should have said "it does not help."
steps.simpleTranslation: And also: רבי יהושע says "he does not need"? He should have said "it does not help"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge from the exact wording of the משנה. This attacks every explanation where the vow is useless because it can be undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Does not need" means there is no worry to begin with. "Does not help" would mean there is a worry but the vow cannot fix it. Since רבי יהושע chose the first wording, Steps 7 and 8 do not fit his words.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: adds another challenge
He does not need to: there is no need at all
It does not help: it would be useless

steps.whatToRemember: Steps 7 and 8 fall. Step 8 clashes with אמימר's ruling, and both clash with רבי יהושע's wording "אינו צריך."

phrases.english: And furthermore, רבי יהושע says:
"He does not need"?
phrases.notes: These are רבי יהושע's words in the משנה about making the husband vow.

phrases.english: He should have said "it does not help"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge, based on wording, against the vow-based explanations.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanations in Steps 7 and 8 that רבי יהושע holds the vow is useless because it can be undone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "אינו צריך" means no need, not uselessness. With those explanations he should have said "אינו מועיל."

steps.title: Final answer: they argue about undoing a הקדש through שאלה
steps.stepSummary: Rather, the two sages argue about whether one may ask a חכם to undo a declaration of הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here they argue about asking a חכם to undo a הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the vow-based explanations, the גמרא gives its final explanation of the argument. It is about undoing a הקדש through שאלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a הקדש cannot be undone through שאלה, the husband's only way to get the property back is to plot with his wife, so רבי אליעזר requires the vow. If it can be undone, there is no reason to plot, so רבי יהושע says the vow is not needed. This fits the wording "אינו צריך."

keyTerms.meaning: Asking a חכם to undo a vow or declaration
Asking a חכם to undo a declaration of הקדש

steps.whatToRemember: Final view: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about whether a הקדש can be undone through שאלה. Whether there is a reason to plot depends on that.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explanation answers both challenges. It does not touch אמימר's rule about vows, and it explains why רבי יהושע said "not needed."

phrases.english: Rather, here
they argue about asking to undo a הקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanations of Steps 7 and 8 after the challenges of Steps 9 and 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about whether the husband's vow (public, or על דעת רבים) can be undone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about whether a הקדש can be undone through שאלה, which decides whether there is any reason to plot.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about שאלה בהקדש.

steps.title: A ברייתא links the two sages to בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says their views match בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if a man consecrates all his property while he still owes his wife her כתובה, רבי אליעזר says that when he divorces her he must vow not to benefit from her. רבי יהושע says he does not need to. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון said: these are exactly the views of בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support its last answer, that the two sages argue about undoing a הקדש. The ברייתא connects their argument to an older argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11 the גמרא said the argument is about undoing a declaration of הקדש. Now it shows a ברייתא where רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says רבי אליעזר follows בית שמאי and רבי יהושע follows בית הלל. The next line will explain which argument of theirs he means.

keyTerms.meaning: One who declares all his property holy (given to the Temple)
The money a husband owes his wife if he divorces her
He must make a vow forbidding himself to benefit from her
These are exactly the same as

phrases.english: And it is taught: one who consecrates his property
and he owed a wife's marriage contract,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
when he divorces her, he must vow against benefit,
Rabbi Yehoshua says: he does not need to,
and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon said:
these are exactly the words of Beit Shammai,
these are exactly the words of Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about undoing a הקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון connects them to בית שמאי and בית הלל.

steps.title: The argument is about הקדש made by mistake
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי hold that a mistaken הקדש still counts; בית הלל hold it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: For בית שמאי say: a הקדש made by mistake is still הקדש. And בית הלל say: a הקדש made by mistake is not הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains which argument of בית שמאי and בית הלל it meant. It is their argument about a הקדש made by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, the man is stuck with his הקדש, so he might plot with his wife instead, and רבי אליעזר requires a vow. For בית הלל, a mistaken הקדש does not hold, so he has a simple way out, and רבי יהושע says no vow is needed. This backs up Step 11: the real question is whether a הקדש can be undone.

keyTerms.meaning: A declaration of holiness made by mistake
It does not count as holy

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר = בית שמאי (mistaken הקדש still counts, so a vow is needed). רבי יהושע = בית הלל (mistaken הקדש does not count, so no vow is needed).

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: הֶקְדֵּשׁ טָעוּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: For Beit Shammai say: consecration in error is consecration,
and Beit Hillel say:
consecration in error is not consecration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the link made in Step 12 and closes the discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two sages argue about whether a הקדש can be undone, matching בית שמאי and בית הלל on mistaken הקדש.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling and the story of רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a guarantor of a כתובה and starts a story about משה בר עצרי and his son רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and so did רבן שמעון בן גמליאל say, etc. משה בר עצרי was the guarantor of his daughter-in-law's כתובה. His son רב הונא was a young Torah scholar, and he was short of money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about a guarantor of a כתובה. It sets up a story that will show how this rule works in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that even when a guarantor will pay the כתובה, the husband must vow when he divorces, so the couple can't plot against the guarantor. Here the guarantor is the husband's own father, and the husband needs money. This sets up אביי's idea in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor, someone who promises to pay if the main person does not
His daughter-in-law
A young Torah scholar
He was hard-pressed (short of money)

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: And so Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel would say, etc.
phrases.notes: He ruled that even with a guarantor for the כתובה, the husband must vow when he divorces her.

phrases.aramaic: מֹשֶׁה בַּר עַצְרִי עָרְבָא דְּכַלְּתֵיהּ הֲוָה,
phrases.english: Moshe bar Atzrei was the guarantor for his daughter-in-law,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן הֲוָה,
phrases.english: and Rav Huna his son was a young Torah scholar,
and he was hard-pressed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with a guarantor, a divorcing husband must vow against benefit from his wife.

steps.title: אביי suggests a plan to help רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests that רב הונא divorce his wife, she collect her כתובה from his father, and then he remarry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Is there no one who will advise רב הונא to divorce his wife, let her claim her כתובה from his father, and then take her back?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a clever way for רב הונא to get money from his father through the כתובה. This sets up רבא's objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the father guaranteed the כתובה, a divorce would make the father pay. If רב הונא then remarries her, the couple keeps the money. This is exactly the kind of plotting the משנה worries about.

keyTerms.meaning: Advice
His wife
And take her back (remarry her)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֵיכָּא דְּנַסְּבֵיהּ עֵצָה לְרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Abaye said: Is there no one to give advice to Rav Huna,
that he should divorce his wife
and she should claim her marriage contract from his father,
phrases.notes: "His father" means רב הונא's father, משה בר עצרי, the guarantor.

phrases.english: and he should take her back again?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֵיכָּא דְּנַסְּבֵיהּ עֵצָה לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with אביי's suggestion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי suggests divorce, collecting the כתובה from the guarantor, and remarriage.

steps.title: רבא objects: the משנה requires a vow
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the משנה requires the husband to vow against benefit, so he could not remarry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But we learned in the משנה that he must vow against benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's plan using the משנה. If רב הונא must vow, he can never take his wife back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow in the משנה exists to stop exactly this kind of plan. A man who vows never to benefit from his wife cannot remarry her. So אביי's advice seems to break the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned (in the משנה)

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But we learned "he must vow against benefit"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהָאֲנַן ״יִדּוֹר הֲנָאָה״ תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's suggestion in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's plan to divorce and remarry.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires a vow against benefit, which blocks remarriage.

steps.title: אביי: he can divorce outside of בית דין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains אביי's view: not every divorce happens in בית דין, so he could divorce without being made to vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי? Does everyone who divorces do it in בית דין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives אביי's answer to רבא. רב הונא could divorce privately, where no one would force him to vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow is forced on him by the court when the divorce comes before it. If he divorces outside בית דין, no one makes him vow. Then he would still be allowed to remarry her.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a question that rejects an assumption)
A court (בית דין)

phrases.english: And Abaye? Is that to say that anyone who divorces
divorces in court?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּיֵי — אַטּוּ כֹּל דִּמְגָרֵשׁ בְּבֵי דִינָא מְגָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the vow only applies to a divorce done in בית דין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every divorce brings a forced vow, so remarriage is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: A divorce done outside בית דין brings no forced vow, so remarriage stays possible.

steps.title: רב הונא turns out to be a כהן
steps.stepSummary: In the end it was found that רב הונא was a כהן, so he could not remarry his divorced wife. אביי says poverty follows the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end it came out that he was a כהן. אביי said: poverty follows the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: the plan could never have worked, because a כהן may not marry a divorced woman, even his own ex-wife. אביי sums it up with a saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with a way around the vow, a כהן who divorces his wife can never take her back. So רב הונא had no way out of his poverty through this plan. אביי's saying means it is hard to lift a poor person out of being poor.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter became known
A priest, who may not marry a divorced woman
Poverty follows the poor

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's plan failed not because of the vow, but because רב הונא was a כהן and could never remarry a divorced woman.

phrases.english: In the end the matter came out that he was a priest.
phrases.notes: A כהן may not marry a divorced woman, so after a divorce he could never take her back.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בָּתַר עַנְיָא אָזְלָא עַנְיוּתָא.
phrases.english: Abaye said: poverty follows the poor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun in Step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The plan was impossible since רב הונא was a כהן; אביי remarks that poverty follows the poor.

steps.title: Did אביי really give such tricky advice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction. אביי himself said that someone who gives clever advice to get around another person's intentions is a רשע ערום, so how could he advise רב הונא to squeeze money out of his father?
steps.simpleTranslation: Would אביי really say this? Didn't אביי say: who is a sly, wicked person? Someone who advises another to sell property, following the view of רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's advice from Step 15 by quoting another teaching of אביי that seems to clash with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's plan used a trick to make the father pay the כתובה, which goes against what the father meant when he became a guarantor. Elsewhere אביי calls a person who gives advice that legally works but goes against someone's intentions a רשע ערום. So אביי seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? This is a challenge that sets up a contradiction
A sly, clever wicked person who does wrong in a way that is technically allowed
One who gives advice
Property

phrases.english: And did Abaye really say this?
phrases.notes: This is about אביי's advice in Step 15: divorce, collect from the father, then remarry.

phrases.english: But didn't Abaye say:
Who is a sly, wicked person?
This is one who gives advice
to sell property,
phrases.notes: This is property given to someone with the condition that after him it goes to a second person.

phrases.english: following the view of Rabban Gamliel.
phrases.notes: This refers to the view that such a sale holds, so the second person cannot take the property back.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר אַבָּיֵי הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to אביי's advice from Step 15 and questions whether it was proper.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's advice that רב הונא divorce his wife so she could collect from his father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי himself condemns people who advise using a legal loophole against someone's intentions, and that is just what his own advice did to the father.

steps.title: A son and a Torah scholar are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this case is special: the guarantor is the father of the one who gains, and the one who gains is a young Torah scholar.
steps.simpleTranslation: His son is different, and a young Torah scholar is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by showing why אביי's advice here is not the kind of trick he condemned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father would not mind his own son benefiting from his money, since the son will inherit him anyway. Also, it is proper to help a צורבא מרבנן so he can keep learning. So this is not the wicked trickery אביי spoke against.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different, a special case
His son
A young Torah scholar

phrases.english: His son is different,
phrases.notes: The guarantor is רב הונא's own father, who would not mind helping his son.

phrases.english: and a young Torah scholar is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a father helping his son who is a Torah scholar is not the condemned kind of trick.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי's advice looked like the sly advice he himself called wicked.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the father would gladly help his son, and helping a צורבא מרבנן is proper, the advice was fine.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's condemnation of the רשע ערום does not apply when a father helps his own son who is a Torah scholar.

steps.title: A guarantor of a כתובה is not bound to pay anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new problem with אביי's plan itself. A guarantor of a כתובה is not legally bound to pay, so the wife could never have collected from the father, and the plan would not work in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him conclude it from the rule that a guarantor of a כתובה is not legally bound!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole plan from a different angle: the father as guarantor would not have to pay the כתובה at all. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's plan depends on the wife collecting her כתובה from the father, the guarantor. But there is a rule that a guarantor of a כתובה is not legally bound to pay. If so, the plan could never work, and there was no need to discuss the vow (Steps 16-17) at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it, meaning there is a simpler reason already available
A guarantor
Marriage contract, the money a wife collects at divorce or her husband's death
Legally bound to pay

phrases.english: But let him conclude it
phrases.notes: Meaning: there is a simpler reason אביי's plan would never work.

phrases.english: from the rule that a guarantor of a marriage contract is not legally bound!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּעָרֵב דִּכְתוּבָּה לָא מִשְׁתַּעְבַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether the advice was proper to whether it could work at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's plan for the wife to collect her כתובה from רב הונא's father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a guarantor of a כתובה is not bound to pay, the wife could not collect from the father at all, so the plan fails before the vow question even arises.
